galleryCards.summary: A mecha dances between two fruits to Dance with Fruits; the motion comes from a Three.js scene driven by the track's low band. To make your own version, change one fruit or the character (humanoid only). Genobi's agent edits only that region of the first still with FLUX 3 Klein, then re-renders the windows it appears in with LTX-2.5 Layout-to-Render. The rig and its moves stay the same. Nothing is rendered without a quote and your yes.

pipeline.step: Window 0 of the 9 s Dance with Fruits loop: the fruit-mecha explode study, 193 frames at 24 fps, band gain auto, release 12, motion gain 1; writes rgb.webm, depth.webm, control.wav, keyframes.json with regions.robot, regions.fruit-left, regions.fruit-right on the 1024x576 guide

One first still per character, exactly 16:9 and aligned with frame 0: a region edit of regions.robot (suggested box = the rectangle scaled to the still, padded about 10 percent) or an owner still in the mecha's pose
One render per character to 2048x1152, CFG 1, seed 42, the loop's first 8.04 s muxed

The swap edit: one render per loop, cut on the measured grid (loop 9.0 s, beat 0.592 s), Nokia cards over beats 13 and 14, drop-beat swap at beat 8 with a typed overlay, 4-frame pixel ramps, the 9 s loop tiled as the audio (sample-aligned; the tripled wav is 60 ms off)

galleryCards.summary: The camera falls between skyscrapers into a cathedral, a crowded hall and a small recording booth, and the sound follows each room. The existing cut's pictures are LTX-2.5 Layout-to-Render shots; its sound is the original track processed on CPU with each scene's geometric impulse response. The AKUSPACE LoRA was tested separately and did not make this cut's audio; that learned room-audio route is experimental and would need more training. To make your own version, change one space: its look, its dimensions, or a room reference image. Genobi's agent rebuilds that room, recomputes its reverb when the geometry changes, and re-renders that one window. Nothing is rendered without a quote and your yes.

pipeline.step: Capture each room study: towers-descent, cathedral-gallery or cathedral-gallery-grow, party-walls (13 x 16 x 5.5 m hall), studio-walls (3.2 x 2.4 x 2.5 m booth); window starts 0, 8.0417, 15.6916, 23.6083 s; writes rgb.webm, depth.webm, control.wav, room-wet.wav
pipeline.tool: Three.js World Builder study (capture.mjs) with CPU Acoustics and Reverb

pipeline.step: Mix room-wet.wav under the dry excerpt (dry 0.9, wet 0.7)
Stitch towers, cathedral, hall, booth; lay the full track over the cut with each window's wet reverb at its start time

No recapture; the reverb stays the same

Recapture, which gives a new room-wet.wav
Re-render and re-mix that window
Propose an editable primitive-room approximation of the reference as a design target, not a metric scan, for the person to review
Then as roomDimensions
Recapture all four windows; wall studies start on quiet frames
Re-render all four
Re-mix the reverb
Replace the source slot or reference image in the project; the rendered clip is unchanged
